chapter: Failure in St. Louis and the Omaha bands
title: Musicians taken into black homes; jazz not commercial
summary: Musicians were taken in and fed by families, and Thompson says he owes his career to listeners because jazz is not commercial music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: But getting back to the St. Louis story, as I said most entertainers, musicians, in the old days, in the black community, if they had any personality at all, the people learned to like you. Not just because you were a musician but as I said you learned how to live with people, and you realize that it was quite a compliment to have people like you and help you, and you needed assistance, and it wasn't uncommon that people would often take you in their homes as a part of the family, you know.

And you know, if you didn't have any money they realized that you didn't work regularly and they would wait until you got the money to pay for the rent or you'd sort of go -- you know, what they call -- what do they call it, Dutch lunch.
You know, when you go Dutch.

You put in, and everybody chip in and buy some food or something like that. And it was not uncommon that people would be that kind to you, which is all the more reason why I said I'm more appreciative of the public as a general, particularly people who like my music. Because all of my life it has been the people who have liked my music who have made it possible for me to continue on to play music. Because the type of music that I play, and that I like to play, which is known as jazz or created music from the soul of your imagination, which is done more or less spasmodically and simultaneously at the time that you're on the job or playing an engagement, you know, it's not the type of music that is considered commercial.
You know. People don't normally pay people to play that kind of music, you see.
Yes. It isn't everybody that appreciates it that hears it.
Right. Like I told you about the girl that thought it was noise.
